summary: PR #710 (60633eff3) implemented the proposal. The backend writes `http-bound` and `http-serving` frames as newline-delimited JSON on the inherited fd 4 telemetry pipe, and `http-serving` is written only after `HttpRouter.serve` has attached the handlers. The desktop validates frames with the shared parser and settles readiness on `http-serving` (source 'protocol'). It also rejects on a port mismatch or a `fatal` frame. The 'Listening on' log detector stays as a second signal. The HTTP probe no longer races from t=0: it starts only after a 3 s fallback delay and is cancelled when a signal arrives. The startup gate (httpStartupGate.ts) holds early probe requests and replays them, so the old 0.9 s dead window is gone. A suppressed or changed log line (RYCO_LOG_LEVEL=Warning, disableListenLog, format change) therefore no longer delays packaged desktop readiness. I found no runtime regression. Remaining nits: there is no server-side test of the http-serving frame. The dev script boot-report.mjs still keys on the log text. In the very unlikely case that fd 4 is unusable and the log line is suppressed, the probe now starts at 3 s rather than at 0.

evidence.note: writeDesktopLifecycleFrame writes NDJSON frames to the attached fd 4 channel. It is best effort and a no-op outside desktop mode.
The channel is attached whenever the bootstrap envelope says mode=desktop and desktopTelemetryFd=4. The desktop always sends this (main.ts:3163).
initializeDesktopResourceTelemetry opens Socket({fd:4}) and calls attachDesktopLifecycleChannel.

httpServingLayer writes {type:'http-serving', port} at line 721. At line 805 it is provided with HttpRouter.serve(makeRoutesLayer), so the frame comes only after the request/upgrade handlers are attached.
The optional http-bound frame is written after bind, together with early static serving. The desktop uses it to load the window early (main.ts:3035-3039).
The DesktopBackendLifecycleFrame union and parseDesktopBackendLifecycleFrame (line 135) validate the port range and bound the text length.
Every non-'sample' line on the shared pipe goes through the shared parser and is passed to onFrame.

A BackendReadinessTracker is created per child before the envelope is written. The telemetry pipe is attached with handleBackendFrame (lines 3251-3256). The pipe always exists because backendLauncher.ts:26 sets STDIO to [ignore, pipe, pipe, pipe, pipe].
handleFrame settles with 'protocol' on a matching http-serving port and fails on a port mismatch or a fatal frame. The log detector is kept as a fallback at lines 60-68.
The HTTP probe starts only after httpFallbackDelayMs and is cancelled when a signal arrives. In the old code at f1be4abc7 it started at t=0 and in parallel.
The startup gate holds requests that arrive in the bind window and replays them when the handlers attach. A late probe no longer pays a full 1 s request-timeout cycle.
Backend stdout is fed to the log detector only while not ready, so log text is not on the primary path.

Desktop tests cover: frames parsed by the shared parser drive readiness, port mismatch, fatal frames, settle-once, and the log fallback. backendStartupReadiness.test.ts:90-115 covers the delayed probe.
A dev diagnostics script still detects 'Listening on' in server.log to measure boot time. This is not on the runtime path.

fixDefects: No functional defects. Minor points only. (1) There is no server-side test that `http-serving` is written with the bound port after HttpRouter.serve attaches handlers. A refactor of the layer ordering in server.ts:715-805 could move the frame earlier without any test failing. (2) If the fd 4 channel is unusable (server Socket construction throws, which is caught silently at DesktopResourceTelemetry.ts:94, or the desktop gets no Duplex at main.ts:3252) AND the log line is suppressed, readiness now waits for the 3 s-delayed probe. Before, the probe ran from t=0 at about +0.9 s. This needs two unlikely failures at once. (3) The comment at backendStartupReadiness.ts:9-12 ('after a readiness signal exists') is ambiguous; the timer starts when the wait begins. (4) boot-report.mjs:107 still measures boot from the log text.
implementationSketch: Optional hardening, not required. (a) Add a server test (for example next to the server layer tests) that attaches a PassThrough via attachDesktopLifecycleChannel, builds the server layer with an ephemeral port, and asserts that an `http-serving` frame with the bound port is written only after a request to a router route succeeds. Detach with detachDesktopLifecycleChannelForTests. (b) In apps/desktop/scripts/boot-report.mjs, prefer the desktop log's `desktop.backend.http-serving` startup phase and keep 'Listening on' as a fallback. (c) Optionally reword the httpFallbackDelayMs doc comment in backendStartupReadiness.ts.
decisionReason: Desktop-internal readiness only. No auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle or Hub protocol involvement.
